title: Common atmospheric pollutants and their sources

final_note: You worked through Common atmospheric pollutants and their sources — 9 specification statements.

concepts.def: The burning of a fuel in oxygen, which releases energy. The combustion of fuels is a major source of atmospheric pollutants.
A substance released into the atmosphere that harms human health or the environment. Burning fuels is a major source of these substances.
Most fuels, including coal, contain carbon and/or hydrogen. Some fuels also contain a small amount of sulfur.
Sulfur is present as an impurity in some fuels, such as coal. It is not a part of every fuel, so not every fuel produces sulfur dioxide when it burns.
Burning in a plentiful supply of oxygen. Carbon in the fuel is oxidised to carbon dioxide and hydrogen in the fuel is oxidised to water vapour.

Burning when the supply of oxygen is too small for the fuel to burn completely. As well as carbon dioxide and water vapour, carbon monoxide, solid carbon particles (soot) and unburned hydrocarbons may be released.
Carbon monoxide, CO, is produced when a fuel containing carbon burns in a supply of oxygen that is too small for complete combustion, so the carbon is only partly oxidised.
Soot is solid particles of carbon released when a fuel burns in too little oxygen and some of the carbon in the fuel is not oxidised at all.
Sulfur present as an impurity in the fuel is oxidised when the fuel burns: S + O2 → SO2. Fuels with no sulfur in them do not produce sulfur dioxide.

concepts.term: How oxides of nitrogen are produced
concepts.def: At the high temperatures reached inside an engine, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together to form oxides of nitrogen. The nitrogen comes from the air, not from the fuel.
Solid particles and unburned hydrocarbons released when a fuel is burned form particulates in the atmosphere.
Fuel molecules that leave the engine or burner without reacting. Together with solid particles they form particulates in the atmosphere.

Work from two pieces of information: which elements the fuel contains, and how much oxygen is available. Carbon gives carbon dioxide, and also carbon monoxide and carbon particles if oxygen is limited; hydrogen gives water vapour; sulfur gives sulfur dioxide; a high temperature in air gives oxides of nitrogen.
Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas. It is colourless and odourless and so is not easily detected.
Rain made acidic by sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen released into the atmosphere when fuels are burned.
Breathing problems caused in humans by sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen in the air.
A reduction in the amount of sunlight reaching the Earth's surface, caused by particulates in the atmosphere.
As well as causing global dimming, particulates in the air cause health problems for humans.

mcqs.q: Air above a busy city contains carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide and particulates. What do these three pollutants have in common?
options: They are all gases formed by incomplete combustion
They are all produced from sulfur impurities in fuels
They are all formed from nitrogen and oxygen in air
They are all released by the combustion of fuels
mcqs.explain: The specification names the combustion of fuels as a major source of atmospheric pollutants, and all three are produced when fuels burn.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the composition of most fuels?
options: They contain carbon and/or hydrogen and always contain sulfur
They contain carbon and nitrogen and may also contain sulfur
They contain carbon and/or hydrogen and may contain sulfur
They contain sulfur and oxygen and may also contain hydrogen
mcqs.explain: This is what the specification states: most fuels, including coal, contain carbon and/or hydrogen and may also contain some sulfur.

mcqs.q: A hydrocarbon fuel that contains no sulfur is burned in a plentiful supply of air. Which substances are released?
options: Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide only
Carbon dioxide and water vapour only
Carbon dioxide, water vapour, sulfur dioxide
Carbon monoxide and water vapour only
mcqs.explain: With plenty of oxygen the carbon is fully oxidised to carbon dioxide and the hydrogen to water vapour; there is no sulfur, so no sulfur dioxide.

mcqs.q: Carbon monoxide is found in the exhaust gases of a petrol engine. Why is it produced?
options: The fuel contains impurities that cannot be burned fully in air
The oxygen supply is too small for the fuel to burn completely
The carbon in the fuel reacts with nitrogen from the hot air
Carbon always forms carbon monoxide before carbon dioxide
mcqs.explain: Carbon monoxide is a product of incomplete combustion, which happens when there is not enough oxygen to oxidise all the carbon to carbon dioxide.

mcqs.q: Oxides of nitrogen are formed inside a car engine. Where does the nitrogen come from, and why does it react?
options: From nitrogen compounds in the fuel, which are oxidised as it burns
From the fuel, because incomplete combustion releases it from the fuel
From the air, because nitrogen dissolves in the water vapour formed
From the air, because the high temperature makes it react with oxygen
mcqs.explain: At the high temperatures reached inside the engine, nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together to form oxides of nitrogen.

mcqs.q: A power station burns coal that contains a small amount of sulfur. How is sulfur dioxide produced?
options: The sulfur in the coal is oxidised to sulfur dioxide as the coal burns
The coal burns incompletely, so sulfur dioxide escapes from the coal
Sulfur in the air is oxidised at the high temperature of the furnace
Carbon dioxide from the burning coal reacts with sulfur in the air
mcqs.explain: Sulfur present as an impurity in the fuel reacts with oxygen when the fuel burns: S + O2 → SO2.

mcqs.q: Black soot is deposited around the burner of a poorly adjusted gas heater. What is soot, and how has it formed?
options: Solid carbon particles, formed by burning in too little oxygen
A colourless gas, formed by burning in too little oxygen
Solid carbon particles, formed when carbon reacts with nitrogen
Solid sulfur particles, formed from the sulfur impurity in the fuel
mcqs.explain: When the oxygen supply is limited, some carbon in the fuel is not oxidised at all and is released as solid carbon particles.

mcqs.q: A fuel oil contains carbon, hydrogen and a small amount of sulfur. It is burned in a plentiful supply of air. Which products are formed?
options: Carbon monoxide, water vapour and sulfur dioxide
Carbon dioxide, water vapour and carbon particles
Carbon dioxide, water vapour and oxides of sulfur
Carbon dioxide, water vapour and sulfur dioxide
mcqs.explain: With plenty of air, carbon is oxidised to carbon dioxide, hydrogen to water vapour and the sulfur impurity to sulfur dioxide.

mcqs.q: Coke is a fuel that is almost pure carbon. A sample is burned in a limited supply of air. Which products would you expect?
options: Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and water vapour
Carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon particles
Carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and carbon particles
Carbon monoxide and carbon particles only
mcqs.explain: With carbon as the only element present and a limited air supply, the carbon is oxidised to a mixture of carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, and some is released unburned as particles.

mcqs.q: An engine burns sulfur-free petrol in a plentiful supply of air. Which pollutant is still likely to be released, and where does it come from?
options: Sulfur dioxide, from the sulfur present in the petrol
Carbon monoxide, from the carbon in the petrol
Oxides of nitrogen, from the air drawn into the engine
Soot particles, from petrol that leaves unburned
mcqs.explain: Neither removing sulfur nor supplying plenty of air prevents nitrogen and oxygen in the air reacting at the high temperature inside the engine.

mcqs.q: Homes with gas boilers are advised to fit a carbon monoxide alarm. Why can people not rely on their own senses instead?
options: It has a faint smell that most people do not recognise
It has no colour and no smell, so it is not easily detected
It is a solid particulate, so it settles out of the air
It is only harmful to people who already have asthma
mcqs.explain: The specification states that carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless and so is not easily detected, which is why it is so hazardous.

mcqs.q: Which pair of pollutants released by burning fuels causes acid rain?
options: Carbon monoxide and oxides of nitrogen
Carbon dioxide and sulfur dioxide
Carbon dioxide and particulates
Sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
mcqs.explain: These are the two pollutants the specification names as causes of acid rain.

mcqs.q: Air beside a busy road contains sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen. What harm do these gases do to people who breathe them in?
options: They cause respiratory problems in humans
They are harmless unless dissolved in rain
They are toxic but cannot be detected at all
They cause global dimming above large cities
mcqs.explain: The specification states that sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen cause respiratory problems in humans as well as acid rain.

mcqs.q: Which two effects does the specification link to particulates in the atmosphere?
options: Acid rain and health problems for humans
Global warming and health problems for humans
Global dimming and health problems for humans
Global dimming and acid rain in nearby areas
mcqs.explain: These are exactly the two effects the specification gives for particulates.

options: Less sunlight reaches the Earth's surface
The Sun gives out less light than before
The average temperature of the Earth rises
Rainwater slowly becomes more acidic
mcqs.explain: Global dimming is the reduction in sunlight reaching the surface, and the specification attributes it to particulates.

mcqs.q: A diesel engine releases solid carbon particles and unburned hydrocarbons. What do these form in the atmosphere, and what do they cause?
options: Acid rain, which damages trees and lakes
Particulates, which cause global dimming
Carbon dioxide, which causes global warming
A toxic gas that is not easily detected
mcqs.explain: The specification states that solid particles and unburned hydrocarbons form particulates, and that particulates cause global dimming and health problems.
